title: 30-Year Treasury Bond auction (January reopening) — 1:00pm ET, the third and final sale of the November 2026 bond, on a Wednesday because settlement is Friday the 15th
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes, PDF CreationDate D:20260804173209-04'00'), FlateDecode streams inflated per page and rows rebuilt from Tm coordinates independently of the proposal that discovered this event. The page-3 row reads verbatim `30-Year  BOND / R / Thursday, January 07, 2027 / Wednesday, January 13, 2027 / Friday, January 15, 2027` — the `R` marks a REOPENING. The two sibling legs read from the same page: `3-Year  NOTE` (no `R`, a NEW issue) auctions Monday, January 11, and `10-Year  NOTE / R` auctions Tuesday, January 12; all three settle Friday, January 15, 2027. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2027-01-07 coupon announcement. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICALISED 2026-09-09 from `proposals/treasury-30y-bond-2027-01-13.from-treasury-30y-bond-2026-12-10.json` (the only proposal for this id), read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md; its date, reopening read, settle date and $22B size expectation all reproduce against a fresh page-by-page parse of the same primary. THE PROPOSAL'S ONE OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THERE IS NO ANOMALY. It flagged the Wednesday slot — 'a compressed Mon/Tue/Wed shape whose driver a never-assessed session on this id should establish rather than inherit'. The driver is settlement arithmetic and it is dated: since 2017-01-01, ZERO of 117 nominal 30-Year auctions have settled fewer than TWO business days after the auction (`api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov` auctions_query, pulled 2026-09-09; the last 1-business-day gap was 2016-04-14, and there were 17 of them, all 2010-2016). Settlement is Friday 2027-01-15 — the 15th, itself a business day — so two business days back is Wednesday 01-13; a Thursday 01-14 auction would be a 1-business-day gap the modern convention has not produced in ten years. The block therefore compresses to Mon/Tue/Wed, which is CONTIGUOUS — more conventional than the December block it follows, which skipped Wednesday 12-09. Wednesday is also not rare in the series at all: 23 of 211 nominal 30-Years since 2009, and January specifically runs 13 Thursdays, 3 Wednesdays (2015-01-14, 2021-01-13, 2025-01-08) and 1 Tuesday (2026-01-13). THE EXACT STRUCTURAL PRECEDENT IS 2021-01-13: same day of month, same weekday, same second reopening of a November bond, same Friday-the-15th settlement, same 2-business-day gap; it cleared bid-to-cover 2.47. THIS IS THE SECOND (FINAL) REOPENING, AND JANUARY ALWAYS IS: all 17 January nominal 30-Years since 2009 are reopenings at cycle position 2 — a calendar identity, since November is the refunding new issue, December the first reopening and January the second. EXPECTED SIZE $22B, on the same grid the December sibling established: 20 consecutive completed reopenings at exactly $22,000,000,000 from 2024-03-13 through 2026-07-09, with 2026-09-10 announced at $22B as the 21st; the separate new-issue grid is $25B and must never be read across. ONE STATISTIC THIS EVENT DECOMPOSES RATHER THAN CORRECTS: the December sibling's pooled 'accepted-offering mean $1.51B, positive 16 of 20' reproduces exactly here, but it is a mixture of two very different populations — across those same 20 auctions the FIRST reopening's SOMA add-on averages $0.19B (6 of 10 positive) and the SECOND reopening's averages $2.83B (10 of 10 positive), a ~15x gap. This event is a second reopening, so its null total-accepted is ~$24.8B, not ~$23.5B. Demand itself shows no such split: within-CUSIP, the second reopening minus the first is -0.017 bid-to-cover across 69 pairs since 2009 (31/69 positive) — a null, not a fatigue effect. THE CORRIDOR IS UNMAPPED, NOT EMPTY, and that is this event's live risk: only 6 tracked entries sit within +/-5 days and none is `high`, but this calendar carries NO 2027 CPI, PPI, jobs or retail-sales entry of any date (CPI coverage stops at 2026-12-10). BLS's own CPI release schedule, read 2026-09-09, also stops at November-2026 data, so the December-2026 print is genuinely undated by any primary today — but its own archive shows the January print landed ON the January 30-Year auction's session in 4 of the last 6 years (2021-01-13, 2023-01-12, 2024-01-11, 2026-01-13). TWO dated adjacent events PROPOSED in the same PR, both read from the same schedule page: `treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-07` (this event's own confirming primary) and `treasury-3y-note-2027-01-11` (the block's NEW-issue leg). Deliberately NOT proposed: `treasury-10y-note-2027-01-12`, already owned by `proposals/treasury-10y-note-2027-01-12.from-treasury-10y-note-2026-12-08.json`, and any 2027 CPI entry, which no primary dates. Reading it, not trading it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed. Ledger: docs/research/events/treasury-30y-bond-2027-01-13.md
